questions.q: What does the `--install` flag do in `helm upgrade --install myapp-prod ./myapp`?
options: Deletes any existing release before creating a new one from scratch
Creates the release if it doesn't already exist, and upgrades it if it does — one command handles both cases
Only works for the very first deploy; later upgrades require a separate helm create command
Forces a rollback to revision 1 before applying the new chart
questions.explain: --install lets the same command serve as both the first deploy and every later upgrade: Helm creates the release if it's missing, upgrades it if it already exists.

questions.q: What does `--atomic` do during a `helm upgrade`?
options: Prevents helm from ever being run twice against the same release
Permanently deletes the release's revision history
Skips the --wait check entirely to make upgrades finish faster
Automatically rolls the release back to its previous working state if the upgrade fails or the wait times out
questions.explain: --atomic is the safety net: a failed upgrade or a readiness timeout triggers an automatic rollback instead of leaving the cluster in a half-upgraded state.

questions.q: What does `helm history myapp-prod --namespace prod` show you?
options: An ordered, queryable record of every revision deployed to that release, with its chart version, app version, and status
A live log of every HTTP request handled by the application
A list of every container image ever pulled onto the cluster's nodes
The Kubernetes API server's audit log
questions.explain: Every install/upgrade/rollback against a release creates a numbered revision, and helm history lists them with when they happened, what chart/app version they used, and their status.

questions.q: When you run `helm rollback myapp-prod 2`, what actually happens to the release's history?
options: It deletes every revision recorded after revision 2
It reinstalls the chart from a remote chart repository, ignoring whatever is on the cluster
It re-applies revision 2's manifests and values as a brand-new revision, without erasing any earlier history
Nothing happens unless --atomic was set on the original upgrade
questions.explain: A rollback adds to history rather than erasing it — it re-applies an earlier revision's state as the next new revision, the same way an upgrade does.

questions.q: What is `helm get values myapp-prod --namespace prod` most useful for?
options: Showing the Kubernetes events generated by the release's Pods
Printing exactly which values are actually in effect for that running release right now
Deleting values.yaml from the chart
Showing a diff between two different chart versions
questions.explain: helm get values shows the merged, effective values currently applied to a live release — the most reliable way to check what's really running when it might not match values.yaml alone.
